chapter: Studio recordings of the late twenties and thirties
title: Red Nichols's Five Pennies personnel and Manny Klein
summary: He reads the personnel of a Five Pennies session; Kline notes Manny Klein dubbed taps in From Here to Eternity.

story.theme_name: Jazz musicians in the movies and film scoring
story.community_name: Jazz musicians on film and studio scoring

blocks.x: Yeah. This is a list of some of the Red Nichols recordings that you made.
Red Nichols and his Five Pennies.
Leo Condilli, trumpet. Miff Moll, trombone; Dudley Fosdick, mellophone; Fud Livingston, clarinet; tenor; Art Miller, string bass. Chauncey Morehouse, drums, vibes, sometimes solo.
Do you remember Manny Klein? He's still playing. I think he's still around, isn't he.
Really. Do you remember anything about him?
Well he was a very good player.
Yeah. There is one story about Manny Klein. I don't know if you know this or not. Do you remember a movie years ago, From Here to Eternity?

It was a movie with Montomery Clift and Frank Sinatra. Do you remember that movie? The reason I mentioned it is because Manny Klein played the trumpet, the bugle on the sound track. He dubbed it for Montgomery Clift. Manny Klein played the taps beautifully.
He played it beautifully. A lot of people don't know that. You were with Red Nichols and His Five Pennies for several recordings.
